ideas.title: Wind an iron stator: the motor gets strong enough for a wheel
ideas.critique: This is the third motor-bench post in a row. If the film is once more a fixed camera on a rotor turning, it reads as 'the motor, now faster'. The strong part is underneath: saturating soft iron magnetised by the coil's own current, I²R heat pulling the pots down, and a turns-versus-torque trade-off the player tunes. That is a real machine-design choice and the cart's core part.

ideas.title: Cells that tire: the pots sag when the motor pulls
ideas.critique: Concentration polarisation with a limiting current from D·C/δ is honest electrochemistry and road step 1. On film, though, it is the same pots and motor, only slower for a moment, so a viewer sees almost nothing new. The battery becomes something to design, but the payoff is invisible apart from a slight dip in motor speed.

ideas.title: Crank it backwards: the dynamo lights a wire
ideas.critique: Back-torque you feel in your own crank when the circuit closes is the first time the island's electricity pushes back on the player. Motional EMF from the existing motor.jl is general rather than a rig. The glowing wire repeats 'Where I rushed it', and it only works if Lumi's crank pose reads as real effort, not as a disc turning by itself.

ideas.title: Planté's accumulator: two lead sheets in acid
ideas.critique: Plates that grow brown by Faraday's law, a Nernst voltage, gassing that becomes rising bubbles in path-traced glass, and capacity that grows with each forming cycle: real chemistry with a visible state and a reason to come back. The danger is a single-plate rig with the PbO2 growth rate written in to land on a nice capacity, and filming it as yet another fixed jar left alone.

ideas.title: The cart drives on its own parts
ideas.critique: This is the big goal itself, but it rests on a stator, an accumulator and a switch, and none of them exist yet. Made now, it would have to fake the strong motor and the stored charge, which turns the core into a rig. The pitch says nothing new about the belt or rolling resistance beyond 'they balance'.

ideas.title: A knife switch Lumi throws
ideas.critique: A blue arc from ½LI² and a stutter from Holm contact resistance are nice details, and Lumi's wing really pulling a handle serves the tinkering the human asked for. It is a small part with one action, and the arc will likely be a look triggered by an energy number, not a simulated discharge.

ideas.title: A galvanometer from a compass and a coil
ideas.critique: A needle swinging in a coil's field is almost 'A compass in a bowl' again, filmed the same way. Real instruments instead of charge bars are the right principle, but as a post it is the most predictable thing on the list.

ideas.title: Brake down the dune, charge the plates
ideas.critique: Regenerative braking only exists once there is a cart, an accumulator and a real dune, and none of them exist yet. Pitched now, it is a step with nothing to stand on. When it does come, an EMF-above-jar-voltage threshold falls out of the circuit for free, which is the good part.

ideas.title: The windmill charges overnight
ideas.critique: Real night wind setting tomorrow's charge is the big goal's daily-return hook, and sail area as a choice gives it depth. It needs a dynamo and lead plates that do not exist yet, so a first version would likely charge a number in a jar, with the rotor's torque from a coefficient written in rather than the flow.

ideas.title: Gears for the dune
ideas.critique: Meshing gear bodies by contact would be new mechanics. It only means something once a motor's torque curve meets a dune slope, and the island has neither yet. A ratio as a multiplier on an axle would be the plain version and the likely one.
